data.narrative:
NextSilicon, a Series B frontier semiconductor company founded by Elad Raz, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 8 private and 3 public peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, and Cerebras on the private side, and ALAB, NVDA, and AMD publicly.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the company's $200M+ total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $380M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series A), Rebellions ($2.3B, Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series A), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 18.4x across the three public semiconductors) is not applicable due to absence of disclosed revenue data.

Triangulation of applicable methods supports a valuation range of $323M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median point of $1.2B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity within the peer set and stage-specific volatility in frontier semiconductor valuations. Key uncertainties include actual revenue generation, technology differentiation relative to comparables, and capital efficiency relative to deployment across the $200M raised to date.
